thread:
Maya: seeing ~150 tiny-gang pods stuck pending in eu-west1c after maintenance window at 02:00. anyone seen similar?
Jon: yep, stacktrace in traces shows a big scheduling delay. pods kept pending, then a burst of evictions when nodes came back.
Li: quick look: maintenance hit a whole rack, kubelet toggled NotReady -> controller drained -> pods evicted. our NVLink soft-affinity then prevented placement because warm pool nodes are in different racks.
Sam: so packing failed because scheduler prefers intra-rack NVLink locality for these jobs. once the rack went away, there weren't enough contiguous slots elsewhere.
Maya: cost side — noticed autoscaler spun up on-demand, drove up short-term bill. estimated delta ~ $2.4k for the 30m flare.
Paul: ops note: maintenance was a NIC firmware update that temporarily disabled link training on several hosts. it was scheduled across the AZ rather than staggered across racks.
Ops: confirmed — we scheduled an AZ-level maintenance to reduce ops complexity, will follow up on staggering.
Jon: short-term mitigation proposals: 1) relax NVLink weight for tiny-gang class 2) allow cross-rack placement if warm-pool nodes available 3) descheduler job to consolidate when nodes healthy
Li: also consider increasing warm-pool spread to have at least one warm node per rack for this SKU. provisioning lead time is ~10m though.
Sam: can we reduce per-pod gpu request for these micro-workers? many are testing 0.25GPUs, maybe safe to run 0.125 in non-critical batches. improves binpacking.
Maya: any quick button we can press now?
Jon: I can push a scheduler canary to reduce NVLink affinity weight from +10 -> +2 for selector label tiny-gang. will monitor pending count + eviction rate.
Paul: I recommend also adding a temporary taint on flaky nodes instead of letting kubelet auto-drain, to avoid evicting locality-dependent pods unnecessarily.
Li: taint example: kubectl taint nodes node-?? thermal=maint:NoSchedule --overwrite. but remember taint will block all new placement, might force more on-demand.
Sam: alternative: have scheduler fallback policy that allows "best-effort-cross-rack" placement if placement fails for X seconds. less churn than tainting.
Maya: which metrics to alert on after canary?
Jon: pending tiny-gang pods > 30 for 10m, eviction spikes > 40/min, and cross-AZ traffic increase (network egress) as a safety check.
Sched-bot: canary deploy-nvlink-relax-171601 started -> 1/4 hosts updated
Jon: rolling now. will post updates in 5m.
Maya: longer term: rack-aware warm-pool + maintenance-stagger policy + scheduler fallback. can we add that to roadmap?
Paul: i'll capture infra ops action to stagger maintenance windows and propose a policy doc.
Li: also open to a descheduler that prefers coalescing tiny-gang onto fewer racks post-recovery to reduce fragmentation.
Sam: agreed. send a short blameless incident note once we have evict counts.
Maya: thanks team, keep an eye on the canary outputs. if no improvement after 10m we'll revert. :thumbsup:
Sched-bot: [deploy-nvlink-relax-171601] 2/4 hosts updated -> monitoring OK
Jon: early numbers look promising — pending down from 150->40 in 6m, evictions dropping.
Maya: great, leaving followups to Paul and Li for runbook + warm-pool plan.
